en: The Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas, the Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
5. The Story of the Elephant-Palace “An elephant of noble gait is yours,
with its head adorned with various jewels.”
Radiant, strong, and endowed with speed,
he glides through the sky;
lotus-like, with eyes like lotus petals.
Wearing the radiance of lotuses and water lilies,
his body strewn with lotus pollen,
he wore a garland of golden lotuses.
A path strewn with lotuses,
adorned with lotus petals,
standing there, lovely and enchanting.
The elephant walks with measured step; as he departs,
his golden bells ring out with a delightful sound.
A sound is heard from them,
like that of a fivefold musical ensemble,
upon the back of that elephant.
Well-clad and adorned,
you outshine a great host of celestial nymphs in beauty.
This is the fruit of your giving,
or else of your virtue,
or else of your act of salutation with joined palms.
"Tell that to me when you are asked.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was delighted.
When questioned, she gave an answer concerning the fruit of that deed:
"Having seen one endowed with virtues..."
I gave a seat strewn with flowers and covered with cloth to one who was meditating, delighting in jhāna, and mindful.
I scattered half of the lotus garland all around the seat with petals.
With their own hands, they were full of faith.
For that one skilled in karma,
this is my kind of fruit.
I am honored and revered by the gods;
indeed, I am one who has attained right liberation.
To a practitioner of the holy life who has come,
one with faith should offer a seat;
thus one shall rejoice, just as I do.
Therefore, indeed, by one who desires their own welfare and longs for greatness,
a seat should be offered.
“Of those who bear their final body.
This concludes the fifth chapter, the *Kuñjaravimāna*.
